Product Title: Jeans Motherhood Maternity
Review: I really like these jeans but the sizing is off. I bought both the small and medium to compare and see which which sizing felt best to me. I'm a size 4 prepregnancy and according to the chart should be a small but am generally between sizes so ordered both just in case, and I'm glad I did. The jeans are stretchy and I like the medium wash but the small pair I received is bigger than the medium pair. (See photos) The colors are slightly different too with the medium being a bit lighter than the small but not a big difference. I tried on the medium first and was surprised to see they felt a bit tight (still wearable but tighter than I would have thought/preferred). I wasn't even going to bother trying on the small but realized the small looked bigger than the medium so tried on and they felt similar but a bit loser than the medium. I then measured them because I thought that was odd and sure enough the small is bigger. I double checked the tags inside and the sizing is correct and the styles are identical so not sure what happened. Length fits me great - I'm 5'2'' and debated ordering petite but glad I ordered the regular instead. I wanted to purchase another pair in a different color as well but can't due to not knowing wht size to order!

Product Title: Jeans Motherhood Maternity
Review: For $18 I am thrilled with these maternity pants! I’m just approaching 20 weeks and my bump finally started to pop. I’m not someone who wears jeans a lot, but figured I needed at least one pair to get through the rest of winter and spring. Still, I couldn’t imagine spending $40-$50 on jeans I would only wear a handful of times. These fit the bill!The belly band part is extremely comfortable- snug enough to fit me now with just a tiny bump but with plenty of room to grow with me! Im folding the belly band in half in the meantime and it seems to work great! At 5’3” they are just a touch long and the ankles are a little baggy but still fit much better than I was expecting- I have that issue with almost any jeans I buy! My biggest complaint is that I do have a decent booty so the seam where the jeans meet the belly band feels a bit low, like i can’t quite get them all the way over my butt. Overall, I’m very pleased with these jeans for the price and they’ll be great to have on hand for the rare occasion I do wear them!For reference, pre pregnancy I was a 2 or XS for most pants, initial pregnant weight gain pushed me into a 4 regular jeans and I JUST outgrew them at 20 weeks. I ordered a small and they fit great!

Product Title: Jeans Motherhood Maternity
Review: These jeans are ok, but beware if you are tall! I'm 5'8 and they land above my ankle so not true "skinny jeans" that you could tuck into low boots but fine for tennis shoes or rolling up. They're also a little bulky around the hips and the tag in the back is very scratchy. Keeping them because I needed something in a pinch but wouldn't buy again.

Product Title: Jeans Motherhood Maternity
Review: One of the most annoying things about maternity pants is that some mediums are HUGE and some are very small. These are smaller than I expected. I’m hoping they stretch out a bit after extended wearing, then I can maintain them by washing on cool.

Product Title: Jeans Motherhood Maternity
Review: The GoodI really do like the fact that these jeans look like regular pants, my husband didn't even notice they were maternity jeans until he saw me taking them off several weeks later.  They're a dark wash and the color has survived many washes (being pregnant makes me sweaty and I wash my clothes much more than I had before I hit the second trimester).  The back pockets are functional, BUT...The BadThe pockets in the back do indeed work but the elastic that goes around my belly doesn't do a whole lot to keep these up.  When I put my phone in my back pocket (and I do this often because I listen to audiobooks and use headphones for phone calls) it weighs my pants down.  I can't keep my phone there without having to pull up my pants constantly, even if I'm not moving around very much.  Even with my phone out of my pocket the pants don't stay up for very long.  It's so annoying and embarrassing to have to constantly be pulling them up.  The problem is a little better after they're freshly washed but not more than a couple of hours.I think they're a nice fit, but from the nature of my job and the fact that I can't keep my phone in my back pocket makes me not want to wear them or purchase them again.  I know it's not a size issue because the three other pairs of pants/shorts I purchased were all mediums and don't have this problem.  If you don't move around a whole lot or don't need the pockets then these might work for you.

Product Title: Jeans Motherhood Maternity
Review: I have narrow hips, and found this fit extremely awkward, too awkward to wear. I’m 5’7 and was 150 lbs pre-pregnancy (size 6-8) and I ordered the medium. First, the jeans portion of these is SUPER low (think ultra lo-rise jeans from early 2000’s), and the stretchy tummy part is way too big and stretchy. Second, the legs were a little baggy on me (I was hoping for a more skinny jeans fit). It looked and felt horribly awkward, and when I walked they would slide down.

Product Title: Teclado sem fio Logitech K380 com Conexão Bluetooth Easy-Switch para até 3 dispositivos e Pilha Inclusa - Compatível com PC, Mac, Chrome OS, Android, iOS e Apple TV - Cinza
Review: Avaliação geral:Comprei este telado bluetooth para livrar as portas USB do meu computador e me surpreendi com sua responsividade rápida. Quando hiberna, demora menos de 3 segundos para se reconectar ao computador e mesmo assim ele vai gravando as teclas digitadas na memória para poder mandar todas de uma vez assim que a conexão é restabelecida, evitando o problema de "perder teclas" digitadas nesse meio tempo. De qualquer modo, ele é inteligente o suficiente para não hibernar toda hora, então nunca tive problema de demora de conectividade (até hoje ele só hibernou de fato de um dia para o outro, quando desligo o computador).Embora compacto, ele tem um ótimo peso, que o mantém firme à mesa. As teclas são macias e o ruído emitido é o mesmo de um teclado padrão de laptop, ou seja, não é exatamente silencioso, mas não é um som que incomoda. Para quem gosta de teclas mais baixas, que exigem menos dos dedos durante a digitação, ele é perfeito.Também não tive problemas com ele de teclas sendo "pressionadas" duas ou mais vezes; algo que me era muito frequente em outros teclados bluetooth mais baratos que adquiri no passado.Para parear o bluetooth também foi fácil. Estando com o teclado ligado e o bluetooth do computador também ligado, coloquei para pesquisar e adicionar um novo dispositivo bluetooth. Daí pressionei e segurei a tecla F1 do teclado até ela começar a piscar rápido. Quando o computador identificou o teclado, o selecionei da lista e apareceu um código numérico de 6 dígitos. Apertei os mesmos números, na ordem, no teclado e depois Enter. O teclado foi pareado com sucesso logo em seguida.Também foi super fácil de configurar o leiaute mantendo o idioma do sistema como Português (Brasil): no Windows 11, Configurações > Hora e idioma > Idioma e região > Português (Brasil), menu três pontinhos > Opções de idioma > Scrollar até a seção Teclados > Adicionar um teclado > Estados Unidos (internacional). Ele passa a aparecer como opção de leiaute na barrinha perto do relógio. Também é possível selecioná-lo, caso haja mais de um leiaute cadastrado, pressionando as teclas Start (Win) + Espaço algumas vezes.Ele não tem as teclas Home, End, PageUp e PageDown, mas é possível emular o comportamento de cada uma dessas teclas segurando a tecla "fn" e usando as setinhas esquerda, direita, cima, baixo, respectivamente.No mais, sugiro a instalação do aplicativo LogiOptions+ para maior customização do teclado. As teclas F1-F12, por exemplo, vêm por padrão com o comportamento invertido (função de mídia, como Play, Volume etc, ao invés do comportamento padrão de Ajuda, Refresh etc, que só fica acessível pressionando junto a tecla "fn"). Pelo aplicativo é possível reverter esse comportamento.Contras:As setinhas de navegação ficam um pouco apertadas, então ele não é muito recomendado para jogos (a não ser que você use o WASD).Também gostaria muito que houvesse uma versão dele no formato ABNT2 e tivesse o teclado numérico, mas como uso primariamente para programação, ele me atende muito bem no dia a dia.

Product Title: Teclado sem fio Logitech K380 com Conexão Bluetooth Easy-Switch para até 3 dispositivos e Pilha Inclusa - Compatível com PC, Mac, Chrome OS, Android, iOS e Apple TV - Cinza
Review: Eu estava de olho nesse teclado há muito tempo. Logitech é uma boa marca e dos produtos que tenho, nunca tive problemas. As teclas são arredondadas e, por isso, tem um charme. 5 principais fatores me chamaram a atenção quando decidi comprar (fatores positivos e negativos), sem incluir o preço, porque estava um pouco mais barato que o normal (160 reais).1) O tamanho. É pequeno, pequeno mesmo. Perfeito para ser portátil. Meu maior uso é com o tablet, então precisava de algo igualmente portátil. As dimensões do anúncio estão corretas.2) Sem fio. O teclado funciona via bluetooth e pode conectar com até 3 dispositivos ao mesmo tempo. Excelente se você usar o mesmo teclado para o computador, tablet, celular e etc. Conectar inicialmente é facil e trocar o dispositivo em uso também.3) A cor. Esse tom "areia" é novo. Pelo menos nunca tinha visto quando costumava pesquisar esse modelo. Incrivelmente, por mais que fosse lançamento, estava mais barato que as cores populares. Haviam poucas fotos dessa cor especificamente quando comprei, por isso anexei mais algumas. É um cinza claro, bem neutro e elegante. Fica muito bonito em contraste com a mesa preta ou branca.4) Teclas silenciosas. Esse foi um ponto levemente negativo para mim, que amo o barulho do teclado. Diria que a sensação de teclar é bem parecida com o teclado embutido de um notebook, teclas baixas e silenciosas. Para a maioria das pessoas, esse é um fator super positivo, mas vale a pena ser mencionado.5) O padrão internacional. Esse é o maior problema desse teclado. Não tem abnt2, que é o padrão usado pelo Brasil. Isso significa que as teclas estão em posições diferentes do que a maioria dos teclados que usamos. É estranho, mas facilmente adaptável. Quando usei pela primeira vez, fiquei confusa porque as teclas não estavam correspondendo com os simbolos que saíam. Logo percebi que como meu computador estava configurado em abnt2, mesmo que a tecla não mostrasse um '"ç" por exemplo, se eu apertasse a tecla que geralmente seria o "ç" em um teclado brasileiro, a letra saía. Procurei um video no youtube que me ensinou a mudar, prefiro que as teclas de fato correspondam os simbolos e que eu precise me adaptar do que manter o padrão abnt2 não correspondente as teclas. Dito isso, vi alguns videos que criticavam o teclado por não ter "ç", pois tem sim. Seja no padrão abnt2 ou no internacional. Basta procurar um video que lhe ensine a configuração. Todos os simbolos que usamos existem, alguns só necessitam de uma combinação de teclas para sair.Esse são os fatores mais importantes. Fatores gerais: chegou super rápido, bem embalado, é lindo, portátil e bem útil.

Product Title: Teclado sem fio Logitech K400 Plus TV com Touchpad Integrado, Conexão USB Unifying e Layout ABNT2
Review: PONTOS POSITIVOS1 - Leve;2 - O touch funciona bem, tem os movimentos de pinça e deslizar a página;3 - Três opções para simular o botão direito do mouse(touch + botão esquerdo abaixo do touch + botão amarelo no canto superior esquerdo), dando versatilidade no uso do teclado;4 - Em nenhum momento senti atraso("delay") no uso no PC, TV E VIDEOGAME PLAYSTATION 4;5 - Funciona também para jogar no PLAYSTATION 4. Sim, teclado wireless funciona nos consoles! Mouses wireless TAMBEM! Joguei COD WARZONE e FORTNITE com ele + UM MOUSE GAMER G305 SEM FIO DA LOGITECH, e ambos funcionaram perfeitamente no PS4. Sendo MUITO honesto:  Não senti um atraso que justificasse não usar esse teclado no console. Não senti mesmo que esse k400 plus "prejudicava" meu gameplay.Se tiver algum "delay", eu não percebo. Jogo FPS a mais de 15 anos(Jogo desde o CS 1.6, passei pelos COD, joguei BF4 mais de 6 anos no PC ) e pra mim esse k400 plus tá funcionado bem. Caso você seja um jogador semi-profissional, profissional ou MUITO criterioso, talvez não seja pra você comprar um teclado sem fio pra jogar NO CONSOLE;6 - Software da Logitech, NO PC, permite mudanças de mapeamento de algumas teclas e outros detalhes;7 - Da pra usar o receptor wireless pra conectar OUTRO dispositivo wireless da Logitech que NÃO SEJA DA LINHA GAMER, ou seja: se você tiver um mouse wireless da Logitech, por exemplo, você pode usar esse teclado + o mouse com UM ÚNICO RECEPTOR WIRELESS, basta baixar o programa LOGITECH UNIFYING;8 - Garantia da Logitech é excelente.PONTOS NEGATIVOS1 - Extremamente frágil. É daqueles teclados que, se cair, você já sabe que vai danificar alguma coisa. De todos os produtos que eu já tive da Logitech, que é minha marca favorita quando se trata de periféricos, esse K400 PLUS é o que tem a PIOR qualidade de construção. O plástico é muito maleável, incomoda bastante;2.1 - Teclas MUITO PRÓXIMAS uma das outras e muito pequenas também. O design do produto não foi pensado pra ser usado por todo tipo de mão, algo "universal".2.2 - ATENÇÃO MULHERES COM UNHAS GRANDES: NÃO COMPREM ESSE PRODUTO, POIS VÃO PASSAR RAIVA! Vocês, quando forem acionar uma tecla, a unha vai na maior parte das vezes apertar em outra tecla por elas estarem muito próximas uma das outras.2.3 - ATENÇÃO PESSOAS COM MÃOS GRANDES OU TEM DEDOS "GORDINHOS": Não serve pra vocês se estiverem pensando em produtividade/ jogos. Realmente não serve. Talvez, só pra usar na smart TV ou no PC em tarefas simples, ainda quebre um galho.3- Sua digitação vai ficar mais lenta pelo fato das teclas serem muito juntas. Você vai clicar varias teclas ao mesmo tempo se for digitar da sua maneira padrão. Fica esperto! Minha mão, como mostro na foto, é mais ou menos grande, mas minha sorte é que meus dedos são finos e, mesmo assim, fico no limite do uso "confortável".Minha velocidade de digitação caiu cerca de uns 30% nesse teclado, fora que apagar palavras ficou bem mais recorrente no meu dia a dia, por causa das teclas pequenas induzirem ao erro na digitação;4 - NÃO TEM AJUSTE DE ALTURA! Eu sinceramente não sei por que a Logitech fez uma coisa dessas. Tive que comprar alguns pés adesivos de silicone(veja nas fotos) pra ajustar a altura do teclado. Achei um absurdo isso. A digitação fica EXTREMAMENTE CANSATIVA, PRA MIM, quando usei esse teclado da forma que veio de fábrica, sem poder ajustar a altura. Fica esperto 2;5 - As teclas são silenciosas, mas meio "moles", passando uma sensação de digitação insegura.6 - Você vai precisar usar a tecla FN para utilizar alguns recursos. Exemplo: pra tirar PRINT, você tem que pressionar FN + BACK. É bem chatinho de se acostumar.Conclusão: Não me arrependo da compra, até agora tô gostando desse teclado sem fio e espero não precisar acionar a garantia futuramente. Também espero que a Logitech lance um outro teclado com touch, que corrija esses problemas desse K400 PLUS. Ele realmente é uma mão na roda pra você que não quer ficar o dia todo sentado em uma cadeira, sendo refém de um cabo USB ligado ao seu PC.Fique atento os pontos negativos que mencionei, pois eles podem ser cruciais no seu uso.

Product Title: Teclado sem fio Logitech K400 Plus TV com Touchpad Integrado, Conexão USB Unifying e Layout ABNT2
Review: A foto que estou postando aqui não é do teclado que acabei de comprar na Amazon, mas do modelo (idêntico) que minha esposa e eu estamos usando aqui em casa desde 2016. Compramos outro porque o nosso (mostrado na foto) está começando a envelhecer: a parte central do "touchpad" ficou lisa de tanto esfregarmos o dedo; a tecla F2 (que nem foi tão usada assim) ficou amarelada; e a tecla amarela, que serve para dar "Enter" e que usamos o tempo todo, agora tem de ser apertada com um pouco mais de vigor para funcionar.Por que compramos outro teclado idêntico a esse?(1) Porque usamos um HTPC e, para isso, o K400 Plus é perfeito. Ele pode ser usado em cima de uma mesa, mas não foi feito para isso. Ele foi feito para ser usado no colo, em cima da cama ou do sofá.(2) Porque ele foi usado quase que diariamente durante vários anos e continua funcional. O nosso já caiu no chão (piso de madeira) umas 6 vezes. Os tombos (de uma altura de 60 cm, que é a altura de nossa cama) nunca afetaram seu funcionamento. O uso (moderado) das teclas não apagou sua pintura. O único senão é a tecla amarela, que foi usada milhares de vezes e que eu ainda pretendo tentar consertar se um dia ela perder de vez o contato.Assim, nossa experiência com esse teclado é bastante limitada (uso exclusivo no HTPC), mas durou tempo suficiente para recomendarmos tranquilamente esse teclado se você pretende usá-lo num HTPC. Se pretende usá-lo para outras coisas, recomendo que leia as principais análises de outros clientes da Amazon.Poderia ser melhor? Poderia. Ainda em 2016, ou talvez em 2017, a Logitech oferecia um modelo retroiluminado, o que seria um conforto a mais porque permitiria usar o teclado numa escuridão absoluta. Mas já não vejo esse outro modelo à venda (ao menos aqui no Brasil), o que me faz especular que ele talvez não tenha dado muito certo, talvez pelo consumo excessivo de pilhas ou outro fator. Por falar nisso, as pilhas duram bastante no  K400 Plus, e seu software avisa quando a energia está acabando.

Product Title: Teclado sem fio Logitech K400 Plus TV com Touchpad Integrado, Conexão USB Unifying e Layout ABNT2
Review: Por ser um teclado barato não esperava muita coisa, porém fiquei impressionado com a qualidade. As teclas fazem muito pouco ruido (com um fone de ouvido ele chega a ser imperceptível), é muito simples de instalar e usar e o tamanho é perfeito (não me gera nenhum incomodo). O único ponto negativo é o touch screen do mouse, pois o deslizamento de tela é muito sensível, tanto que eu acabo optando por usar o meu mouse ou o touch do próprio note. Porém eu classifico o teclado como 5 estrelas devido ao fato que ele entrega mais do que é esperado de seu preço.

Review:

 Pontos positivo:1. RGB - Excelente com cores fortes e opções de personalização.2. Construção das teclas - fácil manuseio, vem com teclas abaixo para alterar função e utilizar junto com a tecla FN. Vim de teclado normal e me acostumei RÁPIDO demais.3. Software - no início encontrei alguns bugs, mas mexendo e entendendo melhor vc percebe que é fácil mexer, dá pra usar mais de um efeito ao mesmo tempo, na foto vc consegue perceber que tem 3 efeitos (confete nas laterais, no meio o base em amarelo e abaixo efeito onda, pegando a barra de espaço).4. Tempo de resposta excelente e é gostoso de apertar.Pontos negativos1. Teclas extras com construção fraca - a barra de espaço e botão extra ESC não é tão bem construído quanto o restante das teclas, fazem um barulho grotesco, inclusive substituí e deixei as normais.2. Estabilizadores não são tão bons, com o tempo creia que dê algum problema, apenas quem é exigente vai perceber, com a barra de espaço extra vc vai perceber que estabiliza menos.3. Switchs soldados - não da pra substituir, você que é mais exigente não vai gostar, apesar que os switchs classifico como BONS, tenho certeza que não terei problema por um bom tempo.Comentário final: você que é um cliente mais exigente talvez sinta certo incômodo com alguns detalhes desse teclado, porém quem veio de um teclado red dragon mais em conta ou membrana com certeza vai gostar muito! Enfim creio que valha a pena sim, pesquise bem, não pague mais que 470 R$ nesse teclado (peguei por 459 em oferta). Acerca da entrega da Amazon nada a reclamar, chegou em 3 dias.

Product Title: Teclado sem Fio 850 USB Preto Microsoft - PZ300005
Review: Importante:Primeiro, não há luz de "caps lock" e "num lock". Uma forma oficial de contornar isso é acessando a pagina oficial do teclado e baixar o driver/assistente. Depois de instalado, toda vez que acionar essas teclas, apareça um aviso no canto inferior direito da tela informando por exemplo "caps lock: ativado ou desativado".(windows 10)Sim, o windows reconhece o teclado mesmo se você não instalar o driver, é plug and play, porém para ter o resultado citado acima é necessário instalar o driver/assistente disponível no site oficial. Onde encontro!? Internet ta ai para isso, só procurar não é difícil, como eu disse está na pagina oficial do produto na internet.Curiosidade:Esse mesmo teclado é vendido também com o kit "teclado e mouse", só que na minha opinião não vale apena. Pois o mouse é um li..x...., definitivamente não vale apena pagar a mais por ele. Eu e meu irmão, comprados em anos diferentes e com espaço de tempo grande, os dois mouses tiveram o mesmo problema, duplo click e problema no sroll. Fora que a construção do mouse não é boa e também não é muito confortável para um uso prolongado. Resumindo, o mouse não justifica o preço a mais.Teclado:O teclado sim, é excelente, não vou me estender muito pois já tem muita gente elogiando. Então não perca mais tempo lendo textão chato :DÉ o segundo que eu compro, o meu primeiro nunca deu problema.Garantia de 3 anos, nunca precisei usar mais sempre ouso as pessoas falarem bem da microsoft em relação a garantia.Teclas macias e silenciosas.Teclas de atalho eu adoro.O perfil baixo do teclado é super ergonômico, tem um posicionamento interessante nas teclas mais para o meio do teclado na horizontal, que é normalmente onde mais se usa, é mais baixo, quase imperceptível olhando de cima, só olhando de lado que se consegue vê.Já vem com pilha, como eu já tive outro teclado desse, posso afirmar que dura bastante.Contra:Não tem como comprar o receptor avulso caso você acabe perdendo, não sei se a outro meio de fazer isso em contato direto com a microsoft.Garantia:Caso de qualquer defeito(seja no teclado ou no receptor) você pode acionar a garantia, é o certo a fazer. Como eu já disse, tem garantia de 3 anos, use!! Lembre-se de guardar sua nota fiscal, nenhuma empresa concede garantia sem a comprovação oficial de compra.Por fim, teclado é excelente. Vale sim o preço de 187,80 nesta data.

Utilizo bastante o computador para o trabalho e ainda não vi sinais que indicasse a necessidade de troca das pilhas. Product Title: Combo Teclado e Mouse sem fio Logitech MK235 com Conexão USB, Pilhas Inclusas e Layout ABNT2
Review: O teclado tem uma boa construção, embora não pareceça ser o mais robusto. Para uso do dia-a-dia, home office e estudos, cumpre bem a função. A digitação é boa, embora as teclas não sejam tão espaçadas, mas é mais confortável que a maioria dos teclados de notebook. Sinto falta do "ponto" no teclado numérico, pois pro meu uso no trabalho seria bastante útil, mas é uma questão de costume. Outra função que poderia haver é a luz indicativa das teclas "caps lock", "num. lock" etc. Contudo esse problema pode ser contornado baixando o aplicativo "Logitch Options +" que oferece a opção de habilitar uma indicação visual na tela quando essas teclas são ativadas ou desativadas; outra opção é ativar o som para as teclas de aderência no Windows, é um indicativo sonoro em bip, mas confesso que demora um tempo até saber qual som indica ativação ou desativação - a opção do Options + é mais conveniente. Um ponto de destaque é a duração da bateria, já estou há mais de um ano utilizando diariamente o produto com as baterias inclusas na caixa e não tive nenhum sinal de que estão próximas de acabar (vale dizer que no Option + é possível habilitar um aviso de bateria fraca, mas essa função ainda não pude testar na prática). De modo geral é um ótimo produto, especialmennte considerando a faixa de preço. Acredito que vai agradar a maioria dos usuários de entrada ou médios.

Product Title: Combo Teclado e Mouse sem fio Logitech MK540 com Teclado com Apoio para as Mãos, Teclas de Mídia, USB, Pilha Inclusa e Layout ABNT2, preto
Review: O produto chegou dentro do prazo, não veio com uma embalagem externa então a caixa original sofreu algumas avarias, considero isso um fator positivo pois evita o uso desnecessário e desperdício de material no transporte, mas se você se incomoda é algo a levar em consideração.O teclado é muito bom, engonômico e o apoio para o punho ajuda muito, senti que as dores diminuiram bem. As teclas possuem sensibilidade média, não precisa de bater super forte mas também não são hipersensiveis (nem prometem ser). O barulho é mediano, não me incomoda mas não é super silencioso. Possui o teclado numérico na lateral, algo que acho esssencial e outros botões que facilitam o dia a dia: calculadora, bloqueio de tela, home, controle de volume e controle de vídeo. Possui pézinhos emborrachados que fixam bem o teclado no lugar.O mouse é confortável, não é tão confortável quanto os modelos que possuem apoio para o polegar mas dentro do meu uso está ótimo. Não tive problemas com precisão ou legs, mas utilizei apenas para design não posso comentar sobre a performance para jogos.A instalação foi extremamente simples, só conectei o receptor e liguei os produtos, não tive problemas com conexão entre o computador e o kit, mantenho conectado e quando ligo já saio utilizando. Dentro do mouse tem um espaço para armazenar o receptor para transporte e é ótimo, evita acidentes. Ambos parecem bem resistentes e que vão durar um bom tempo. Foi uma boa compra.

Product Title: TECLADO GAMER RAPID FIRE REVOLUTION USB 2.0 DAZZ
Review: Funcionando todas as teclas. Este teclado é para mim o melhor custo-benefício por esse preço. Base em metal, é um teclado bem pesadinho (portanto não fica deslizando na mesa enquanto você digita ou joga). As teclas são bem suaves e não é tão barulhento. As cores são fixas. Possui um efeito de iluminação (fade in e fade out), controle de velocidade do efeito e 3 níveis de iluminação. Para quem não sabe:- Tecla FN + On/Off = Inicia o efeito (ele fica piscando em fade in e fade out), se clicar novamente o efeito para e a iluminação fica constante (normal).- Tecla FN + '-' (tecla do hífen e underline) = Diminui a velocidade do efeito.- Tecla FN + '=' (tecla do igual ao lado da tecla do underline) = Aumenta a velocidade do efeito.- Tecla FN + Page Up = Aumenta o brilho da iluminação.- Tecla FN + Page Down = Diminui o brilho da iluminação.- Tecla FN + W = Troca as teclas W, A, S e D com as setas do teclado (as setas ficam se tornam W, A, S e D). Para voltar ao normal é só clicar 'FN + W' novamente.O lado negativo é a falta de manual para explicar essas funções.

Product Title: KODAK Câmera digital PIXPRO Zoom FZ55-BK de 16 MP com zoom óptico de 5 x 28 mm de largura angular e tela LCD de 2,7 polegadas (preta)
Review: DISLIKES:  No external charger for the battery.  Most digital cameras I have purchased in the past always came with an external charger.  This one only charges the battery internally, unless you buy an external charger, which I would highly recommend one always have an external charger for extra/spare batteries for your camera!  Also didn't like you only access the manual by reading or downloading on-line.  What is wrong with manufacturers today?  They SHOULD supply manuals with their products, no matter what it is.  Not have the end user go hunting for it, and many times when I went seeking a manual for a product I bought, if the manufacturer may have discontinued the item, they tend to remove the manual, and now it's no longer available to access, even though you may have bought the item new, no manual with it is just dumb and lazy on their part.  If I am printing it on paper, then they sure didn't save any trees, and maybe I had to print it several times before I got the fomatting right to put it in a notebook or folder for future reference, wasting paper and more trees.  Manufactures take notice, you ARE NOT doing the trees or the end user any favor by EXCLUDING manuals from your products!LIKES:  Easy to use, but then I have been accustomed to digital cameras for a very long time, so I can navigate around them very easily, and I found this one very easy to navigateonce I checked out all the buttons and what they did.  Has a nice LCD screen for viewing your photo's after taking the shots, one thing I don't quite understand is the "slideshow", you get 3 options to pick from #1, #2 or #3,  #1 just shows the basic snapshot and really does nothing.  #2 will do some type of effect, as does #3, but to me, they make no rhyme or reason for even being there at all.They don't copy to your computer when transferring the photo's to your computer, you'd have to use another program, like some kind of video editor to create a slide show with similar or like effects.  And the issue is, it's NOT a slide show of the photo's in the camera or on the SD Card, it only affects the ONE PHOTO you're viewing, so it's not a slideshow by any means.  When I selected it to see what it did, it just affected the one photo I was viewing, I had expected to see a slideshow of ALL the photo's I had taken or be allowed to select a specific number to create a slideshow that could be saved as a video exported file from the camera, but none of that is possible.  Waste of a camera resource in my opinion.The photos are good, and I have attached a few here to show the cameras' capability in low light conditions, the two photo's of the same kitten (Cordellia-001/-002) are indoors in low light, the older cat (Apollo), taken outside is nearing sunset.  Forgive the messy look of the floor inside the house, we're in the process of removing the carpeting from our house, and we're just starting work on it, so the floors look a tad messy for the time being.Even with the Dislikes and the few faults it has, I can recommend the camera, it seems to take nice photographs, I haven't tried videos as yet, I have some projects in mind for that for YouTube later on.  I mostly purchased this camera for still photos when on nature walks or other outside activities that may be photo-worthy.

Product Title: Câmera Digital Sony W830 Nova Hd 20.1mp Zoom 8x
Review: The Good:You get real zoom, instead of fake digital zoom on a phone.Image stabilizing works great.Real flash, not a useless LED fake flash on a phone.The Bad:Weak flash compared to other cameras.Slower than other cameras.Not many manual controls, and no quick access to the ones it has.It wants to be an auto-only camera, but it's not very good at its automated jobs (eg brightness, focus, etc).I've been playing with this for a couple weeks. It CAN take nice pictures, but it doesn't want to. It's very erratic with brightness, and you tend to get either very dark areas or very bright areas. Washed out skies are common.The flash has about half the range of a similar Canon model.All of the settings are in a big long list. There is no organization to it. The program vs auto mode option is at the top, but the camera is "smart" enough to remember where you last were on the list of settings, so you might want to switch modes and find you need to click up a bunch of levels to get to the mode select. And when you ARE in the program mode, ALL of the program settings are in this long list. None of the physical buttons are for +/- exposure, ISO, or focus mode. Thankfully the flash setting has a button.Even in program mode, you get limited settings. If you want to force (or should I say suggest) the camera do distant or macro focus, you can only do so by selecting a "scene" such as "food" or "landscape".There is an auto focus assist LED, which is a sort of advanced feature (a spot LED which turns on briefly during focusing so it has something to focus on in dark areas). But you can't force it on, and the camera is bad at figuring out when to use it (I don't know why, it's easy to tell when the view is dark, and there's no harm in using it all the time). In very dark scenes, it will often make a LONG attempt at trying to focus without the assist light first, and only then will it start over with the assist LED.Why Buy This?It's still better than a phone (even a good one) if you want real zoom and image stabilizing. You can record video which doesn't look like a jittery hand is holding a phone. For close photos, it has a real non-blinding strobe type flash.But don't wait forever or pay full price for this. It's one of the lowest-end cameras in the category. You will be better off buying a used Canon.

Product Title: Câmera Digital Sony W830 Nova Hd 20.1mp Zoom 8x
Review: At this price point, we can't expect miracles.  My other camera is a Sony a-6000, but the DSC-W830 was purchased as a simple-to-use camera for my wife--to replace her 2006 model Canon Elph SD600 (6 megapixels, 3x optical zoom, no image stabilization).  The image quality and noise levels are definitely much better than the old Elph with this Sony point-and-shoot.  But the remaining question is whether my wife should use this camera or her iPhone 6 while on vacation.On paper, the DSC-W830 should be better: its sensor is 50% larger than the iPhone sensor, and it boasts 20 megapixels compared to the iPhone 6's 8 megapixels.  And the DSCW830 sports a Zeiss lens.  Using the intelligent auto setting, I shot several scenes using the DSC-W830 (lens at widest setting--25 mm focal length equivalent) and the iPhone 6 (29 mm focal length equivalent) and the standard photo app.  In the centers of the photos, the DSC-W830 images were clearly sharper reflecting the improved resolution of the sensor.  But at the edges of the photos, the iPhone 6 images were much sharper because of the large chromatic aberration for the Sony product.I haven't tried out the P mode on the DSC-W830 in with various settings (exposure compensation, ISO, HDR changes, etc.), and I suspect that by fussing with the Sony camera I could make it perform close to the iPhone 6--in the center of the image with wide angle.  The chromatic aberration appears to be a lens issue, and I haven't tested different focal lengths (levels of zoom) to see whether it gets worse or better when focal length is increased.  The iPhone 6 probably has less of a problem with this because it uses a prime lens (no zoom).  Of course the DSC-W830 has the zoom capability (an advantage), which the iPhone lacks.I tried out the panorama feature on the DSC-W830, and found the resolution of images to be so bad that the panoramas were useless.  The iPhone 6 panoramas are excellent--way, way better.  The SCN setting on the Sony camera may be useful, but the 4 picture effects are gimmicky in my opinion.  The screen menus are simple and easy to navigate.Based on sensor size and number of pixels, I would have thought that the Sony camera might have been better than the iPhone 6, but overall it is equivalent in some circumstances and worse in others.  Did Sony use a cheap sensor and other inexpensive electronics? Is their firmware less sophisticated? I was disappointed in the lens performance (chromatic aberration, softness at the edges of the images).I think that the Sony DSC-W830 is suitable for snapshots made by people who may be technically challenged--Aunt Ida or your 12 year-old pre-teen.  It is convenient if you are going to an amusement park with the family and just want some fun shots.  But if you don't need the zoom, you can probably get comparable to better results with your iPhone 6, particularly if you install the ProCamera 8 app, which makes the iPhone work more like a digital camera.UPDATEPrevious shots were done in the evening, when conditions might have been less than optimal.  I tested the DSC-W830 in bright sunlight and with different zoom settings.  Results were disappointing.  The right edge of the image was blurred at 1X, 2X (equiv. to 50 mm), and 4X zoom.  I had thought that perhaps a smaller aperture (resulting from the bright sunlight) might help, or that the lens would have a "sweet-spot" at mid-zoom.  The blurring would be just detectable with a 4x6 print, but I wouldn't use images from this camera for any greater enlargement of the whole image.  You can have an acceptable enlargement if you crop off the edges leaving the center 50% of the image. One of the photos below (about 1/3 of the whole frame) shows the blurring on the right edge. I'm disappointed.

Review: Terrible picture quality. I had previous good experience with Sony's CyberShot model line and Carl Zeiss lenses, and that's why I bought this to replace my 9-years old Canon PowerShot A400. To my disappointment, not this time!I took the same frame with this camera and my old Canon that I must have put at least 10,000 shots on, compensating for the difference in focal depth by stepping backward for a mere 5-6 feet (the Sony has a wider viewing angle than my poor old Canon). On the surface, both shots looked ok. On 1:1 scale, the details and edges are completely smudged and lost with this Sony. The tired lens of my 9-years old Canon was able to produce a crisper shot overall and captured more fine details of near and far objects in the frame. Mind you, I had both shots set at the same ISO and light conditions. I have uploaded and noted the pictures of the 2 cameras for everyone to see. The should by under Customer Images page http://www.amazon.com/gp/customer-media/product-gallery/B00HNJWUBI/ref=cm_cmu_up_thanks_hdrThen I thought about the difference in Megapixels. The Canon is an old 3.2 MP, this one is 20.1 MP. I'm guessing that the Sony's processor is unable to utilize all these pixels efficiently in the time the camera takes to shoot the image. My experience with older DSC CyberShots have been amazing. But this was also around the time when 4 megapixels was considered high-end for point-n-shoot cameras. So, this is all speculation. But, the bottom line remains: A new camera is unable to produce a crisp, clear, fine detailed image as a 9-years old one with 1/6th the megapixel power and outdated processing technology.I still love an value Carl Zeiss optics. In fact I own several interchangeable lenses from this company and they are superb in every aspect. I just don't understand how Sony managed to smudge this lens's reputation so badly by installing it in this particular model.Another possibility is that this particular camera was a lemon, but I don't have the time or energy to order a replacement just to verify that it was actually this particular piece and not the entire DSCW830 line.Thankfully, it only took me 3 days of testing to make up my mind and decide that I'm not interested in paying for a new camera that gives out pictures that are worse than the one I'm trying to replace. I already started the return/refund process with Amazon and shipped it back yesterday! 5 Stars to Amazon though for their return/refund policies.

Product Title: Câmera digital Sony Cyber-shot DSC-H300
Review: Update June 20, 2019:My second set of NiMH batteries just went flat after taking photo number 1488. So I am getting on average 744 photos per charge on a set of rechargeable NiMH batteries. That is really good battery performance.The Sony DSC-H300 is a very nice camera for the price. It is not equal to a Rebel SLR or my Fuji, but it costs a fraction of the price of either of those.  For a basic point and shoot camera it has a lot going for it.The user interface is about the same as most digital cameras, so you should be able to figure it out. I had very little trouble with it.The complete operator manual is available by going to sony dot com and digging down through support.The photographs are sharp enough. The colors are a bit more saturated than they are in my other cameras, but that is what I have noticed in Sony cameras that I have owned previously.The autofocus can be a bit tricky, but with practice I am mostly able to make it work. I take a lot of macro photos, and sometimes it does better using the area focus, and sometimes it does better using the spot focus. I try things until it works.I was initially put off by the fact that there is no obvious Macro setting.  I take a lot of macro photographs.  However, the camera does have a macro mode; it sets it automatically, removing the need to remember to put it into macro mode before shooting. So the lack of a menu setting for macros is a benifit rather than a deficiency.I also was initially put off by having to set the exposure correction through the menu system. You have to push the menu button, then click down a few spaces to get to the EV setting. It takes four or five menu clicks.  However, once I had set the EV to something other than zero, pushing the Menu button took me directy to the EV menu, so it became a one-click setting at that point. Clever. In fact the menu does that in general. The menu rembembers where it was and takes you back there when you push the Menu button. That memory is reset when you go in and out of replay mode or turn the camera on/off.The camera uses AA batteries, which is a requirement for me. I have boxes of NiMH rechargeables that I use in all of my cameras, and the DSC-H300 works fine with them.  I shot 646 photographs on one set of fully charged Eneloop 1900 mAh NiMH batteries.  That is not an estimate; I actually took that many photos on one set of batteries. It reports the charge level accurately as well.For connection to a computer, the camera uses a Mini USB 5-pin connector, not to be confused with the older USB mini 4-pin connector, which is larger. I have some older cameras that use a connector that is called a "Mini USB", but it is not the same connector as the one that works with this Sony.  The older connector is more accurately referred to as a "Mini USB 4-pin" connector.  Fortunately, the camera came with the proper cable, so this was not an immediate issue, but if you need to replace the cable, make sure that you get the "Mini USB 5-pin" version.A nice feature is that the backup battery that maintains the settings, such as the clock when the main batteries are out is rechargeable. So if you leave the camera with no batteries in it long enough for the backup battery to go flat, you can simply leave fresh AA batteries in it for a while and the backup battery will recharge.  You don't have to buy a replacement cell to put into the camera.One of my favorite features of this camera is that it allows me to decide whether to connect to a computer using Picture Transfer Protocol (PTP) or USB Mass Storage. PTP is a camera-specific protocal that connects to the computer in a readonly fashion. That makes it very unlikely that I can do something stupid and damage the SD card. In PTP mode, unmounting the card just requires turning off the camera.  If you want to change anything on the card using the computer you have the option to connect to the computer as Mass Storage USB. That protocol gives you full access to the SD card. Just be careful to unmount the card before pulling the plug or turning off the camera or you risk damaging the file system on the card and losing your images. I use PTP because it is simpler and safer.The camera connects properly to USB on Windows 7, Linux Mint 18.1 and Linux Mageia 7 Beta 1. Product Title: Câmera digital Sony Cyber-shot DSC-H300
Review: Update June 20, 2019:My second set of NiMH batteries just went flat after taking photo number 1488. So I am getting on average 744 photos per charge on a set of rechargeable NiMH batteries. I try things until it works.I was initially put off by the fact that there is no obvious Macro setting.  I take a lot of macro photographs.  However, the camera does have a macro mode; it sets it automatically, removing the need to remember to put it into macro mode before shooting. So the lack of a menu setting for macros is a benifit rather than a deficiency.I also was initially put off by having to set the exposure correction through the menu system. You have to push the menu button, then click down a few spaces to get to the EV setting. It takes four or five menu clicks.  However, once I had set the EV to something other than zero, pushing the Menu button took me directy to the EV menu, so it became a one-click setting at that point. Clever. In fact the menu does that in general. The menu rembembers where it was and takes you back there when you push the Menu button. That memory is reset when you go in and out of replay mode or turn the camera on/off.The camera uses AA batteries, which is a requirement for me. It reports the charge level accurately as well.For connection to a computer, the camera uses a Mini USB 5-pin connector, not to be confused with the older USB mini 4-pin connector, which is larger. I have some older cameras that use a connector that is called a "Mini USB", but it is not the same connector as the one that works with this Sony.  The older connector is more accurately referred to as a "Mini USB 4-pin" connector.  Fortunately, the camera came with the proper cable, so this was not an immediate issue, but if you need to replace the cable, make sure that you get the "Mini USB 5-pin" version.A nice feature is that the backup battery that maintains the settings, such as the clock when the main batteries are out is rechargeable. PTP is a camera-specific protocal that connects to the computer in a readonly fashion. That makes it very unlikely that I can do something stupid and damage the SD card. In PTP mode, unmounting the card just requires turning off the camera.  If you want to change anything on the card using the computer you have the option to connect to the computer as Mass Storage USB. That protocol gives you full access to the SD card. Just be careful to unmount the card before pulling the plug or turning off the camera or you risk damaging the file system on the card and losing your images. I use PTP because it is simpler and safer.The camera connects properly to USB on Windows 7, Linux Mint 18.1 and Linux Mageia 7 Beta 1. It connects using both USB 2.0 and USB 3.0 ports.Caveat: It is necessary to take off the lens cover before turning on the camera.  When you turn on the camera, the lens moves out slightly, and the lens cap blocks that motion. The instruction manual says that to change a menu setting, find and set the new setting, then push the OK button to select it. However, pushing the OK button makes the menu disappear. If you are setting multiple items in the menu, it is annoying to go back into the menu for each item.  However, you can set multiple items easily. To set multiple items, select the desired item and setting, then push the Down button or the Up button to accept the new setting. The menu will remain displayed, and the new setting will be accepted.So I give high marks to the Sony DSC-H300 as a beginner camera or a less expensive knock-around shop camera. If you are looking to take truly outstanding photographs to print in large format, you might want to look around and spend more. But for a general purpose camera, the DSC-H300 works.

Product Title: Câmera Digital Lumix DMC-ZS80 Panasonic Preta
Review: Did I say I loved this camera?  Well I do.  I love this camera.  When it first arrived I was a little disappointed that it is a little bulkier than my previous cameras.  I've purchased several generations of the Panasonic ZS series and have loved every one.  Well, I was tired of buying refurbs and decided to treat myself to a brand new model, with all the bells and whistles.  This was the first camera I've had without GPS built in.  Initially I was disappointed that I couldn't get one with it, but connecting it with the cell phone's GPS was easy.  On average it's taken about 13 seconds to lock in, the longest was maybe 20 seconds.  I was concerned about when I travel abroad if it would work, but from what I've read, you bring your cell phone and even if you don't have phone or internet service, our US gov't tax dollars provide us with free satellite connections all over the planet. I haven't had the opportunity to test this for myself, but there are a few YouTubers who have confirmed it. ANYWAY this thing takes amazing pictures.  Granted, all digital cameras have their faults when it comes to focus and lighting issues, but for the most part this thing works like a champ and on rare occasions have I run into any of those problems.The screen is crisp and flips up for selfies, and includes a 4-3-2-1 countdown so you can smile and look ready and natural for the shot.  This also worked well when I had to use a mini tripod for a group photo and it 'just' gave me enough time to jump in - although the outtakes are pretty funny with my hair flying in the air as I hadn't quite gotten where I needed to be.  And even THOSE pictures are CRISP.It is such a pleasure to take a Panoramic shot and have all the images stitched right on the camera rather than bringing it home and doing it on the computer.  How nice to see it instantly to ensure you've captured everything you wanted.  I have yet to try it but am anxious to dabble with the burst feature along with another 'stitching' program which takes several photos you've chosen (out of up to 30[?]) and putting them together to show the object-in-motion in a series of positions, while everything else stays the same.  THIS you have to use software for, but it's going to be great, I know it.SUMMARY:  The camera is great.  As far as point-and-shoot cameras go, it is a terrific choice with lots of cool features.  It's a little too big to fit in an average sized pocket but if you wear cargo pants, you can probably carry it in there.  I chose to get a good case with a strap as I decided that most of the time I KNOW when I'll be taking pictures, and will want it out and ready anyway.  The other reason is that these cameras are notorious for getting dust in, behind the lens and will need it cleaned professionally (trust me - as careful as I was it was still a disaster doing it myself).  The GPS will work anywhere and tag all your photos accordingly.  Panoramic shots, you see in an instant!  Burst is terrific too, and the app and/or software will help to make some even more interesting pictures for you to share.  You want this camera.  I have absolutely NO buyer's remorse.

Product Title: Câmera Digital Lumix DMC-ZS80 Panasonic Preta
Review: I was looking for a camera for an upcoming trip to South America. Although my iPhone 13 Pro takes great photos, it has limited telephoto capabilities, so I decided to buy a "real" camera instead, one that was both compact in size but had good optical zoom.After considering both the Panasonic Lumix ZS80 and very similar Nikon Coolpix A1000, I decided to order the Lumix. After playing with it for a couple of days, I decided to return it, primarily for two reasons:1. The fonts on the screen and camera controls are very small, and hard for me to read without reading glasses, which I don't plan to wear outside. That might have become less of an issue after I became more familiar with the camera, but I didn't want to have to struggle with it on my upcoming trip. Note that reading the fonts was not a problem when using the viewfinder rather than the touchscreen.2. The feature that allows you to automatically transfer photos from the camera to your phone using the Panasonic app was pretty quirky. Even though the camera can connect to the phone via Bluetooth, you have to connect the phone to the camera's WiFi in order to transfer photos.A couple of other observations: there are two manuals, basic and advanced. A printed copy of the basic manual is included, but you have to access the advanced online. Also, the cover over the charging and HDMI ports is very flimsy and seems like it might fall off.I can't evaluate the camera's performance since I didn't use it enough. It appears well built (other than the port cover) and feels comfortable in your hand. It's pretty small, so it should be easy to pack. I also ordered a case, extra battery, battery charger, and memory cards (none come with the camera), but returned everything except the memory card that I opened.Sorry it didn't work out for me, but if your eyes are better than mine, the camera is worth considering.

Review: I love this camera. Long zoom. Reasonable lens speed. Excellent software. A ton of features. Great pictures. But half the pictures taken with the flash have a dark shadow in the lower right corner. I tried VERY hard to be aware of the position of my hand relative to the flash and I still partly covered it half the time. How much worse would it be if I was trying to quickly take a picture and not paying careful attention to my hand position?I'm returning it and getting a different camera with a pop-up flash. It doesn't have as much zoom, but hopefully I can take flash pictures without carefully positioning my hands. We'll see.

Product Title: Câmera Digital Lumix DMC-ZS80 Panasonic Preta
Review: This is a fantastic camera - as long as you have never used a DSLR or mirrorless camera with a good sensor.The features are amazing, as is the zoom. The flaw is when you view your pictures larger than 100% - for instance, if you want to take advantage of the high megapixel count, and crop part of the image. Unfortunately, the pictures are highly compressed and upon close inspection are filled with noise and artifacts. They look great zoomed out, but that's it. Even when using RAW format, the images are compressed too much. It needs an uncompressed RAW format, but this is lacking.You can even see the issue when zooming an image on the built-in LCD.I'm told that part of the issue is due to the small sensor - but I've had other much cheaper cameras that did not do this to the photos. Even my iPhone doesn't seem as bad when zooming an image to crop it. I suspect their compression algorithm is too aggressive combined with a small format sensor.The colour and brightness are good. The features in the camera are amazing. It's too bad that what counts (for me) is lacking.Most people will be ok with these images. I have used some much better cameras, and expect better, especially at this price. I need to find a similar camera with a larger sensor, and an uncompressed RAW option.

Product Title: Camera Digital Sony Cyber-shot DSC-WX500
Review: The box includes the WX500 camera, AC adaptor, rechargeable battery pack, micro USB cable, and a wrist strap. I purchased an SDHC memory card and a case separately. I bought the WX500 over the HX90V because I don't think I'll need a pop-up viewfinder or the GPS function. I've heard that everything else is the same, so I might as well get the cheaper option.The camera itself isn't as light as I thought it would be, but it's light enough that I wouldn't mind carrying it everywhere. It's also thicker than I expected, but I'll get used to it. For everything it has to offer, I don't find the thickness or the weight as a big problem.I tried out the movie function, and it's nice. The camera can auto-focus pretty accurately and I love that it doesn't make any sound while focusing. The mic records pretty clearly too. I haven't recorded anything in a noisy environment yet, so I don't know how it'll be like in that situation.You can turn the small wheel on the top through each mode (10 total), and it explains what each setting is for. For example, the "Superior Auto" says "The device beautifully shoots automatically while reducing blurring and noise." It's going to be fun playing with the camera, but even with the descriptions- I'm not really sure when to use to each of the mode. There's not much dramatic difference between each mode. I found the picture effects, under camera settings, to be really fun- especially the partial color effect. It comes out B&W, except the one color that you choose.I was most excited about the screen that flips up. I was actually contemplating between the Sony WX500 and the Samsung NX Mini. I wanted the lenses to be built into the camera (not interchangeable), so I chose the WX500. I'm sure the NX Mini would've been lighter and slimmer, but I feel like the WX500 has more functions to play with. Anyways, the screen flips up well. It has just enough resistance that I can put it at any angle and it'll be stable. What I don't like is that I can't take a picture in selfie mode while looking at the screen because in the photo, it looks like I'm looking up at the sky. But even so, it's very convenient because I can finally position myself and anyone else in the photo. I thought about why there aren't any cameras with a screen that flips down because that would give the same feel as taking selfies on a smartphone. I guess it would look a little weird. I'd make one though, if I could.The 30x zoom is NICE. I took a picture of my mom from really far away, and it looked like I took it right in front of her. I don't know how much I'll use the zoom, but the quality overall is really good.If you're looking for a simple, light camera that has a screen that flips up- I think I would recommend the NX mini.If you're looking for a camera that has a screen that flips up, but also many other functions PLUS 30x zoom- I would recommend the WX500.

Product Title: Camera Digital Sony Cyber-shot DSC-WX500
Review: The WX-500 and it’s sibling the WX-350 take images and video that are overall very similar.  I found the 350 first as an open box item for $175 and purchased it.  The WX-350 lacks MAS-priority controls and an articulating screen and has only a limited number of video modes.  The WX-500 has a variety of video modes and that was important to me because I bought it to do video soccer games etc.  Articulating screen is nice for that as well.  I have a PENTAX K-50 but it’s video is not great.  This quite frankly takes better video.I became frustrated with the WX-350 because of it’s lack of DSLR like controls and returned it and ordered this and I’m much more comfortable with having MAS-Priority modes.  I don’t use my DSLR in auto mode and didn’t want to do that with a P+S either.PROS (both)Image quality (wow)Video quality (wow)Compact SizeBattery Life (much higher than most)CONS (both)Both models only open up to f/3.5 so not much bokeh with either.The screen is not great.  I took some fall foliage pics and on screen looked more brown than orange but on the computer the colors were accurate and popped.  Did some macros as well and didn’t look good on the camera screen but were great on a computer monitor so don’t delete images until seen on your computer.This will probably make a good backpacking camera due to it’s light weight, great image quality and long battery life.  I would recommend the 350 for someone who only wants to point the camera and shoot and doesn’t care about controls.  The 500 is not that much more but offers much more control of settings and is probably better for someone who already has a DSLR and is buying a second camera that is more portable.Update:  Have had it for a while now.  Video is probably it's strongest point for purchasing.  Images at low light and moderately high ISO (think 800+) can become quite noisy.  iPhone actually has lower noise but (if you don't zoom with the iPhone) but the WX500 has lots of optical zoom.  With the WX500 after about 15X zoom finding focus is nearly impossible and there is no manual focus.  IMHO there's no reason to buy anything with more than 15X though.  I've had a number of different P+Ss and NONE could focus well beyond 15X.  LCD screen as others have said is not bright and difficult to see in bright sunlight

Product Title: Camera Digital Sony Cyber-shot DSC-WX500
Review: I really like this camera. I was looking for a perfect compact camera with a super zoom, and the WX500 fit the bill. The camera is small enough to fit into your pocket/purse/fanny pack and has a terrific 30x optical zoom. The camera includes enough manual power to take decent pictures; however, if you're used to a larger camera with more sophisticated innards/software and sensor, the images may sometimes appear a bit weak. The Hi image mode to take multiple images in seconds produces significant noise, so the normal single shutter option yields the best results. I have included some pictures from a park test shoot and a couple from the recent CinemaCon event in Las Vegas. The Red Carpet event where I captured images of Jeff Goldblum and Brent Spiner  are a testament to the zoom capability of the camera. I wasn't allowed near the Red Carpet and had to stand yards away; in addition, I had to capture images of the stars in between photographer rigging and photographers. The camera performed really well in this instance and yielded really nice images (Red Carpet lighting helps too).The camera comes with a wrist strap and I highly recommend that you keep it attached to your camera and wrist as you get used to it, and it does not come with a grip (Optional grips are available on Amazon). It also comes with a wall-USB charger and cable, and the battery charges inside the camera. The battery life seems about average and I didn't find myself wanting for power after an hour-long shoot of constant picture taking (no flash).If you need an ultra-compact camera with a superior zoom, takes decent pictures and has decent battery life, the WX500 is for you.

Also had issues with the battery draining fast while off, did the firmware update and still same issue.  Wasted money on that brand.I reviewed a lot of cameras in this price field and decided to go with this Sony, it's awesome, I love it!!!

Product Title: Camera Digital Sony Cyber-shot DSC-WX500
Review: After I got my DSLR for hobby shooting years ago, I never bothered to get another nice point and shoot because my cell phone camera more than sufficed. But when an MLS team opened up a new stadium (DC United) in my town, I got season tickets. If you’re ever taken pictures at a professional sporting event with your phone, you quickly learn digital zoom is terrible.The stadium doesn’t allow detachable lenses, so the DSLR is out of the question. So I bought this fella purely based off of the positive reviews of its optical zoom which were glowing. And I have to tell you: The optical zoom lives up to the hype.Image stabilization is inconsistent, but good enough. You’ll notice how important stabilization is when you go 30x on a long distance target. Holding a rectangle in your hands is not natural, so if you adjust your hand ever so slightly, you have a blurry picture. But good news: You get used to holding the camera after a while and it becomes less of an issue.I’ve now taken to carrying this camera in my every day carry bag and stopped using my iPhone camera. The ability to upload photos from your camera to phone via the WiFi hotspot the camera makes is super convenient.I’d totally recommend this camera.

Product Title: Camera Digital Sony Cyber-shot DSC-WX500
Review: I've had this for about a year and love it.  The zoom is incredible, makes a fantastic travel camera.  The panorama mode is easy and intuitive.  I use the PlayMemories app occasionally with my android phone to be able to post pics to social media, it connects with NFC and then I can select pics to move via wifi to the phone, pretty slick once I got used to how it works.  The flip screen for selfies is nice, and the timer is easy to use for group pictures.  The amount of time from hitting the power button to being able to shoot is surprisingly quick for having such a big lens to extend.  My most recent trip was 5 days and like 75 pictures each day, the battery finally went down one bar by the end of the trip, I've never been able to actually run the battery down, holds a charge forever.My only gripe is that the camera itself is very slippery to hold onto.  I bough some grip tape (search Amazon for GT-5000 Grip Tape) and cut little strips to put on the camera where I usually hold it and that made a world of difference.

I thought about why there aren't any cameras with a screen that flips down because that would give the same feel as taking selfies on a smartphone. I guess it would look a little weird. I'd make one though, if I could.The 30x zoom is NICE. I took a picture of my mom from really far away, and it looked like I took it right in front of her. I don't know how much I'll use the zoom, but the quality overall is really good.If you're looking for a simple, light camera that has a screen that flips up- I think I would recommend the NX mini.If you're looking for a camera that has a screen that flips up, but also many other functions PLUS 30x zoom- I would recommend the WX500.

Product Title: Camera Digital Sony Cyber-shot DSC-WX500
Review: The WX-500 and it’s sibling the WX-350 take images and video that are overall very similar.  I found the 350 first as an open box item for $175 and purchased it.  The WX-350 lacks MAS-priority controls and an articulating screen and has only a limited number of video modes.  The WX-500 has a variety of video modes and that was important to me because I bought it to do video soccer games etc.  Articulating screen is nice for that as well.  I have a PENTAX K-50 but it’s video is not great.  This quite frankly takes better video.I became frustrated with the WX-350 because of it’s lack of DSLR like controls and returned it and ordered this and I’m much more comfortable with having MAS-Priority modes.  I don’t use my DSLR in auto mode and didn’t want to do that with a P+S either.PROS (both)Image quality (wow)Video quality (wow)Compact SizeBattery Life (much higher than most)CONS (both)Both models only open up to f/3.5 so not much bokeh with either.The screen is not great.  I took some fall foliage pics and on screen looked more brown than orange but on the computer the colors were accurate and popped.  Did some macros as well and didn’t look good on the camera screen but were great on a computer monitor so don’t delete images until seen on your computer.This will probably make a good backpacking camera due to it’s light weight, great image quality and long battery life.  I would recommend the 350 for someone who only wants to point the camera and shoot and doesn’t care about controls.  The 500 is not that much more but offers much more control of settings and is probably better for someone who already has a DSLR and is buying a second camera that is more portable.Update:  Have had it for a while now.  Video is probably it's strongest point for purchasing.  Images at low light and moderately high ISO (think 800+) can become quite noisy.  iPhone actually has lower noise but (if you don't zoom with the iPhone) but the WX500 has lots of optical zoom.  With the WX500 after about 15X zoom finding focus is nearly impossible and there is no manual focus.  IMHO there's no reason to buy anything with more than 15X though.  I've had a number of different P+Ss and NONE could focus well beyond 15X.  LCD screen as others have said is not bright and difficult to see in bright sunlight

Product Title: Camera Digital Sony Cyber-shot DSC-WX500
Review: I really like this camera. I was looking for a perfect compact camera with a super zoom, and the WX500 fit the bill. The camera is small enough to fit into your pocket/purse/fanny pack and has a terrific 30x optical zoom. The camera includes enough manual power to take decent pictures; however, if you're used to a larger camera with more sophisticated innards/software and sensor, the images may sometimes appear a bit weak. The Hi image mode to take multiple images in seconds produces significant noise, so the normal single shutter option yields the best results. I have included some pictures from a park test shoot and a couple from the recent CinemaCon event in Las Vegas. The Red Carpet event where I captured images of Jeff Goldblum and Brent Spiner  are a testament to the zoom capability of the camera. I wasn't allowed near the Red Carpet and had to stand yards away; in addition, I had to capture images of the stars in between photographer rigging and photographers. The camera performed really well in this instance and yielded really nice images (Red Carpet lighting helps too).The camera comes with a wrist strap and I highly recommend that you keep it attached to your camera and wrist as you get used to it, and it does not come with a grip (Optional grips are available on Amazon). It also comes with a wall-USB charger and cable, and the battery charges inside the camera. The battery life seems about average and I didn't find myself wanting for power after an hour-long shoot of constant picture taking (no flash).If you need an ultra-compact camera with a superior zoom, takes decent pictures and has decent battery life, the WX500 is for you.

Product Title: Camera Digital Sony Cyber-shot DSC-WX500
Review: Wow this is an awesome camera! I have spent days playing with it and the zoom on it is pretty incredible! Takes beautiful pics!!! I especially love that you can send the photos wirelessly to your phone, computer or tv.  That's a bonus!! Easy to learn if you read instructions. I had a Nikon which I used 6 times and it suddenly would not work unless the usb AND power brick were attached (not plugged in wall just attached to camera), so picture that, your pretty Nikon with a short usb and power brick dangling from the side of it while you snap a pic.  Ridiculous!  the camera was barely used by only me.  Nikon was no help and I refused to spend more money on it in repairs considering it was new! Also had issues with the battery draining fast while off, did the firmware update and still same issue.  Wasted money on that brand.I reviewed a lot of cameras in this price field and decided to go with this Sony, it's awesome, I love it!!!

Product Title: Camera Digital Sony Cyber-shot DSC-WX500
Review: After I got my DSLR for hobby shooting years ago, I never bothered to get another nice point and shoot because my cell phone camera more than sufficed. But when an MLS team opened up a new stadium (DC United) in my town, I got season tickets. If you’re ever taken pictures at a professional sporting event with your phone, you quickly learn digital zoom is terrible.The stadium doesn’t allow detachable lenses, so the DSLR is out of the question. So I bought this fella purely based off of the positive reviews of its optical zoom which were glowing. And I have to tell you: The optical zoom lives up to the hype.Image stabilization is inconsistent, but good enough. You’ll notice how important stabilization is when you go 30x on a long distance target. Holding a rectangle in your hands is not natural, so if you adjust your hand ever so slightly, you have a blurry picture. But good news: You get used to holding the camera after a while and it becomes less of an issue.I’ve now taken to carrying this camera in my every day carry bag and stopped using my iPhone camera. The ability to upload photos from your camera to phone via the WiFi hotspot the camera makes is super convenient.I’d totally recommend this camera.

Product Title: Camera Digital Sony Cyber-shot DSC-WX500
Review: I've had this for about a year and love it.  The zoom is incredible, makes a fantastic travel camera.  The panorama mode is easy and intuitive.  I use the PlayMemories app occasionally with my android phone to be able to post pics to social media, it connects with NFC and then I can select pics to move via wifi to the phone, pretty slick once I got used to how it works.  The flip screen for selfies is nice, and the timer is easy to use for group pictures.  The amount of time from hitting the power button to being able to shoot is surprisingly quick for having such a big lens to extend.  My most recent trip was 5 days and like 75 pictures each day, the battery finally went down one bar by the end of the trip, I've never been able to actually run the battery down, holds a charge forever.My only gripe is that the camera itself is very slippery to hold onto.  I bough some grip tape (search Amazon for GT-5000 Grip Tape) and cut little strips to put on the camera where I usually hold it and that made a world of difference.
